body:
## Summary

`gdoc write` and `gdoc push` rebuild a document from Markdown: `write`/`push` re-import the whole document through Drive's Markdown importer, and `write --tab` deletes the tab body and re-inserts what `parse_markdown` produces. Markdown cannot represent most native Google Docs structure, so these commands silently discarded it and re-uploaded documents whose content had not changed. This PR makes the rebuild refuse unless everything in scope is on an explicit allowlist, warn when it will only rebuild styles, and skip the upload when the content already matches.

### Deny-by-default rebuild guard

`check_markdown_rebuild` in `gdoc/api/docs.py` inspects the raw document before any delete, insert or upload. The classifier walks every key it reaches and permits only the constructs the rebuild demonstrably round-trips:

| Allowed (rebuilt faithfully) | 
| --- |
| Paragraphs styled as normal text or headings 1-6 |
| Bullet and numbered lists (including the indents the importer generates for them) |
| Inline bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code (Courier New) and URL links |

Anything else blocks with exit 3 and no mutation, and the error names the raw field so the reader can find it in the Docs API: `table`, `footnoteReference`, `headers`, `footers`, `inlineObjects`, `positionedObjects`, `pageBreak`, `columnBreak`, `sectionBreak`, `columnProperties`, `tableOfContents`, `horizontalRule`, `equation`, `autoText`, `richLink`, `person`, `dateElement`, `namedRanges`, `suggested*`, header/footer ids, plus `multiple tabs` and `comment anchors`. Element kinds the Docs API adds later block the same way because they are not on the allowlist. Tables stay blocked until a test proves their round trip. A tab replacement additionally exports the whole tab the way `write --tab` would and parses it back: any paragraph whose text, named style, bullet or allowlisted inline styles do not come back identical at the same positions blocks as `literal Markdown text` or `formatting round-trip`, so text that merely looks like Markdown (`# literal`, `| a |` rows, a code fence) and any exporter gap refuse instead of silently changing content.

**Style overrides warn, they do not block.** Colour, highlight, underline, small caps, fonts other than the code font, explicitly disabled emphasis, alignment, spacing, indents outside lists, other paragraph layout, non-default direction, title and subtitle paragraphs, heading ids (deep links break), links to headings or bookmarks, section-level overrides, adjacent lists that would merge, list formatting the rebuild path does not regenerate (glyphs, formats, marker styles, ruler-moved indents) and named-style definitions that differ from the import defaults print one `WARN: Markdown rebuild will rebuild: ...` line. The list and named-style comparisons use the exact output of each rebuild path, captured live: the Docs UI presets for tab replacements, and hyphen bullets, decimal numbering and the default named styles for whole-document imports. A whole-document rebuild also resets `documentStyle` (verified live: pageless became paged, A4 became US Letter, custom margins, orientation and background were cleared), so it prints a dedicated `WARN: Markdown rebuild will reset page setup to import defaults` line whenever the document differs from what the import leaves behind.

**Scope.** A whole-document rebuild inspects everything. A tab replacement inspects only the target tab and skips that tab's headers, footers and `documentStyle`, since deleting the body range never touches them. Comment anchors anywhere in the document block a tab replacement too, because Drive does not say which tab an anchor belongs to; only comments with a Drive `anchor` count, not the `quotedFileContent` metadata that `comment --quote` stores on unanchored comments.

### `--allow-lossy-rebuild`

New flag on `write` and `push` (and the matching MCP boolean parameter) for disposable documents. It permits structural loss and is independent of `--force` (conflict override) and `--force-collapse-tabs`, which is still required to collapse a multi-tab document. The help text lists the allowlist.

### Skip unchanged uploads

When the Markdown export already equals the content to write, `write`/`push` report a no-op and heal the read baseline without calling the Drive or Docs mutation endpoints. The comparison ignores leading blank lines, trailing whitespace and line endings, which the importer renders as nothing, but keeps first-line indentation, which can turn a paragraph into a code block. The baseline recorded is the version observed before the export, so a concurrent edit can only surface as a conflict on the next write, never be adopted unseen.

### Baseline lint cleanup

A separate mechanical commit clears 196 pre-existing Ruff findings (import ordering, line wrapping, dead f-strings) so `uv run ruff check gdoc/ tests/` passes repository-wide. It does not change any API request payloads.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest tests/` passes (1,748 tests), `uv run ruff check gdoc/ tests/` and `scripts/check-no-stubs.sh` pass.
- `test_rebuild_blocks_every_kind_outside_the_allowlist` feeds every structural, paragraph-element and tab-level kind in the Docs API schema plus an invented future kind and asserts each blocks under its field name; `test_rebuild_allowlist_passes_silently` feeds a document using every allowed construct.
- Tests cover the exact Drive upload parameters and Docs batch requests, unchanged-content no-ops, refusal without state advancement, the no-op baseline under a concurrent edit, and MCP flag mapping.
- Live checks on throwaway documents (trashed afterwards): `write` and `push` on a document with a heading, list, coloured text, end-aligned paragraph and footer exited 3 with zero mutation requests and an unchanged Drive version; a second document confirmed that the Markdown import resets page mode, size, margins, orientation and background.
title: fix: guard lossy Markdown rebuilds and skip unchanged uploads
